annotations.title: Types and properties of an IFC model — what rules to write

description:
CALL THIS FIRST, as soon as the user gives you a token - a link
thenewengineer.com/ia/XXXX pasted in the conversation - BEFORE you
answer anything, even when the user only says they will choose or do
something themselves. It answers within seconds, while the network
graph is still being built - use that time to think.

THE USER WANTS TO CHOOSE THE UNITS THEMSELVES (« let me select »,
« je vais choisir les centrales »): the place to do it is the units
page. Go on through the steps below until trace_duct_circuits (token
only) returns 'lien_centrales', and GIVE THEM THAT LINK. Never tell
them to select « in the interface » without the link: there is no
other place to select.

A MODEL ALREADY TREATED: if the answer carries
'designation_existante', an earlier session already designated the
units and fans of this model. Reuse it: skip step 2, go straight to
trace_duct_circuits, and show the user the designation you reused.
Post new rules only if the user asks to start again.

THE CIRCUITS OF A MODEL IN FOUR CALLS:
  1. read_ifc_overview - this call: the types of the model.
  2. apply_ifc_rules - your rules. Give air handling units,
     monoblocs and ventilation casings the role
     centrale_de_traitement_d_air, fans the role ventilateur, and
     smoke exhaust fans (and smoke compensation fans) the role
     ventilateur_desenfumage, exactly these words - and ONLY to
     equipment that holds a fan.
     Coils, heat exchangers, filters, silencers, dampers, VAV boxes
     are pieces of the network, not units. Its answer lists under
     'equipements' every unit and fan of the model.
  3. trace_duct_circuits with ONLY the token - it computes nothing,
     walks the networks from every unit and fan, and either returns
     the COMPLETE list of units and fans with a view-only page, or
     says the units could not be connected to the model's networks.
  4. trace_duct_circuits again with the units the user wants, or
     all_networks=true for all of them (offered up to 50 air
     networks only).
The answer of this call repeats these steps under 'marche_a_suivre'.

YOU SEE A SAMPLE, THE TOOL SEES EVERYTHING. This overview shows one
example per type, not every piece: you cannot count the units, the
fans or the networks of the model from it, and you must not believe
you have seen them all. The tool applies your rules to every piece
and walks every network. So never pick the networks to compute from
this overview: trace_duct_circuits gives you the complete list of
units and fans first, and you choose from THAT list.

WHAT YOU GET. Not 3 000 parts: an INDEX of the model, one line per
FAMILY of types (the sizes of one family share its line) - dampers,
terminals, equipment, proxies -, each with its IFC class, its number
of pieces, an example GUID and the identity fields of its largest
type ('identite': object_type, nom_du_type...), which is what rules
are written on. Plain ducts and fittings need no role: they are
listed in one line each under 'reseau_ordinaire', and
'cotes_exemples' shows the numeric properties of the main duct
families - where height, width and diameter are.

THE DETAIL, ON DEMAND. When a family's name does not tell you what
it is, call this tool again with families=[its 'famille' names] (up
to 12 per call): you get every property of an example piece and
every type of the family. property_catalogue=true lists every
property of the model once. These follow-up calls bill nothing.

WHAT TO DO WITH IT. Write RULES, not verdicts. For roles: which words,
in which field, identify a fire damper, a silencer, a balancing
damper, an air terminal, an air handling unit, a fan, a pump - and
which groups are NOT network at all (access zones, plinths,
placeholders, damper motors). For sizes: which 'PropertySet.Property'
holds height, width, diameter, length. A rule applies to every part,
including those you were not shown, and to the user's next models.

TRAPS the field 'a_savoir' warns about: values are in the FILE's unit
(see metres_par_unite), not millimetres; insulation sizes and
hydraulic diameters look like dimensions and are not.

The field 'etat_du_graphe' says whether the networks are ready yet:
'pret' means read_ifc_networks will answer now.

families.description: Leave EMPTY on the first call. Then, to read EVERY property of some families, their 'famille' names from the first answer - at most 12 per call. Only the detail asked for comes back.
families.title: Families

property_catalogue.description: True lists every property of the model once, by property set, with an example value - to find which 'PropertySet.Property' holds a size or a flow. Only the catalogue comes back.
property_catalogue.title: Property Catalogue
